scope: Host input execution, capture/worker/encoder/RTP evidence review; offline mocks only

findings.claim: frame_timing precedes encoding/RTP and can attach post-capture input IDs to old or reused frames.
findings.method: Imported bare_track fixture without MSS/native input. Used 2x2 synthetic pixels. Blocked the image worker, applied the exact pending-ID update after frame selection, then released it. Separate case provided only the old ndarray cache.
limits: Proves a causal association defect, not actual native pixel response latency.
frameId is a per-track timing counter without an RTP timestamp or attempt/lease identity.
Even an after-input fresh capture does not by itself prove the operating system has rendered the effect.
No production frame capture or encoding was executed.

findings.claim: Adapter-rejected ordered inputs still enter pending visual IDs because the append is not gated on result status.
findings.method: Actual on_input with fake adapter returning sequence-gap for a command in the matching fixture lease. No native command execution.
limits: Also source-applicable to other adapter results carrying inputIds, including execution-failed or dropped move.
Lease rejection before the adapter returns early and is not this path.
An ID in frame_timing is neither accepted-input proof nor visible-effect proof.

findings.claim: Keyboard result timestamps are both recorded after worker completion, so wire hostExecuteMs overrides the actual adapter-await duration with nearly zero.
findings.method: Actual apply_keyboard with one offline worker sleeping 40ms and returning a synthetic applied result, then actual _wire_execute_ms. No key or native input.
limits: Production values are local adapter-await log values and include queue and scheduling wait.
No corresponding production wire payload was captured; near-zero wire values follow from source and offline reproduction.
Does not change keyboard execution itself; it conceals its cost in latency diagnostics.

findings.claim: Detailed trace encode timing measures generator creation; codec execution occurs during packetize and is attributed to packetize.
findings.method: Actual H264VideoToolboxEncoder.encode and _encode_frame with a fake codec sleeping 40ms and returning a tiny Annex-B NAL; synthetic 2x2 AV frame, no hardware/software codec invocation.
limits: Affects opt-in detailed stage attribution.
Aggregate WRD_ENCODER_SAMPLE elapsed time remains a meaningful overall local wall duration.
It must not be used to conclude that RTP packetization is the encoding bottleneck.

findings.claim: RTP observer records wire binding/send evidence before the underlying DTLS send succeeds; only the first packet of a frame is observed.
findings.method: Installed the real observer into the disposable offline Python process, created a real aiortc DTLS object in NEW state without a transport, and attempted one synthetic RTP packet.
limits: Enabled only by WRD_FRAME_TRACE_DETAIL=1; not established as active in current production.
Correctly observes the RTP header submitted at the send API, not successful emission or complete-frame delivery.
No network packets were transmitted; the real send rejected the disconnected DTLS state.

nativeGrab.meaning: MSS grab interval on the background capture thread; detailed trace only in the reviewed telemetry path

capturePrepareMs.meaning: Worker preparation: np.frombuffer/reshape and resize for fresh frames; cache copy or zero fill for reused/fallback frames. Excludes MSS grab, screenshot age, worker queue, AV frame construction.

frameConvertMs.meaning: AV VideoFrame construction/copy and any conversion fallback; excludes screenshot preparation.

imgprocQueueMs.meaning: Submission timestamp to worker start, including executor/scheduling delay.

imgprocBuildMs.meaning: Preparation plus frame construction; overlaps capturePrepareMs and frameConvertMs.

recvTotal.meaning: Track recv wall time, including pacing, queue, worker work and coroutine resumption; excludes later encode and RTP. capture_wait is deliberately zero, not evidence that MSS grab costs zero.

encodeTotal.meaning: Local encoder entry to packetization completion; includes actual codec work and packetization. Overlaps encode and packetize; current split is wrong because _encode_frame is lazy.

rtpSendMs.meaning: null is appropriate; no completed-send duration is provided here.

exclusions: Do not sum build+prepare+construct or encode_total+encode+packetize.
Do not sum marginal p50/p95 across frames.
Grab operates concurrently with prior output/encoding; timing values are not all sequential.
Detailed trace has no implemented standalone reformat recording in the reviewed encoder.
RTP timestamp identifies media ordering and is not a cross-machine capture wall clock.

limits: Current source normal Host uses the 1x factory; no claim that 2x capture causes the incident.
Running-process source identity was not independently revalidated during this subtask.
These are separate telemetry windows, not frame-aligned pipeline sums or matched A/B tests.
Encoder and construct means are weighted by their respective frame counts; output FPS is the median of capture-output windows.
Wall durations include scheduling/preemption and are not pure CPU time.
No normal production grab/age/worker-queue/RTP completed-send measurements can be reconstructed from these aggregate lines.
Event-loop maxima come from threshold-triggered logs, not a complete latency distribution.
No input text, coordinates, raw production input IDs, tokens or SDP are retained.
